findings.title: Initialization can be front-run
findings.description: The InitStore instruction initializes a singleton PDA that holds the OApp configuration and registers the OApp with LayerZero, also setting the admin. This instruction can only be invoked once, but it is vulnerable to front-running if the program deployment and OApp initialization are not executed within the same transaction. The root cause is the lack of atomicity between deployment and initialization, allowing an attacker to observe and preempt the initialization transaction. An attacker could exploit this by monitoring the mempool for the initialization transaction and submitting their own with a higher gas fee, thereby becoming the admin of the OApp. The impact of a successful exploit is that the OApp could be initialized with a malicious administrator and potentially incorrect LayerZero endpoint addresses, which would require redeployment to fix, leading to operational disruption and potential trust issues.

findings.title: Ambiguous state initialization
findings.description: Both the Solana and EVM example OApps store received messages in permanent storage, initializing the message variable with the default string "Nothing received yet." This creates ambiguity because the state of a newly initialized OApp is indistinguishable from the state of an OApp that has received a message with that exact content. The root cause is the use of a sentinel value that overlaps with valid input space, rather than using an explicit state indicator. An attacker or malicious actor could send a message containing "Nothing received yet." and create confusion about whether a message was actually received. While this does not lead to direct financial loss or critical system failure in the example, it sets a poor precedent for developers who may copy this pattern into production systems, where such ambiguity could lead to incorrect state interpretation and flawed logic. The impact is primarily on code quality and developer guidance, making it an informational issue.
